# ductnetwork steady solve — method specification for an independent reference

This file, with `cases.json`, is everything a reference implementation needs. It states the model the page `ductnetwork.html` (manifest revision `2026-10-16.ductnetwork-4`) documents, and, where its documentation is silent, the law its code applies, written as equations. Sources are marked **[Learn]** (the page's in-tool Learn topics), **[Limitations]** (manifest `limitations.en`), **[Message]** (a sentence the page shows the user) and **[Code]** (the law the page applies where no text states it). Section 12 lists every ambiguity found.

## Revision 2026-10-16

No model, graded value or refusal kind changed. The import refusal for a file that is not valid JSON now reads "The file is not valid JSON: <browser parser text>" (§8, kind `invalid_json` unchanged), and every message and status sentence is shown in the page language; graded outputs are the kinds of §8 and §9, which do not depend on the language.

## Revision 2026-10-15

The page was changed at revision `2026-10-15.ductnetwork-3`; the clauses below were edited to match, and `cases.json` lists the same changes in `spec_changes`.

| change | clauses edited | cases added | cases whose graded outputs change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sj_range` also fires for ε/D_h < 1e-6, ε = 0 included; both bounds 1e-6 and 1e-2 are inside the range | §9, A1, A3 | `sj_eps_bounds` | `correlation_range_flags` (duct R4) |
| Node pressures are gauge pressures relative to the outdoor air at the node's own elevation; the energy balance carries (ρ − ρ_out)·g·z with ρ_out = ρ, so elevation does not change any solution | §3, §6, A4 | `riser_open_both_ends`, `riser_small_drive`, `elevation_invariance` | `duct_elevation_riser`, `partial_load_demand`, `random_mesh_B` |
| The fan curve is stated as the fan total-pressure rise in Learn, field labels, limitations and report text in all seven languages; no number changes | §4, A5, §10 | `fan_total_pressure_basis`, `fan_basis_documentation` | none |

## 1. Model and units

Steady, incompressible, constant-density airflow network **[Limitations]**. Unknowns: the airflow of every component and the gauge total pressure of every free node; both are solved simultaneously **[Learn: intro, solver]**.

| quantity | unit in the document | unit in the equations below |
|---|---|---|
| airflow (demand, `Qrated`, `Qdesign`) | m³/h | m³/s (divide by 3600) |
| pressure (`p`, `P0`, `Prated`, `dpDesign`) | Pa (gauge) | Pa |
| duct/tee section `W`, `H`, `D`; roughness `eps` | mm | m (divide by 1000) |
| length `L`, elevation `z` | m | m |
| density `rho` | kg/m³ | kg/m³ |
| kinematic viscosity `nu` | m²/s | m²/s |
| `opening`, `speed`, `loadFactor`, `speedFactor` | % | fraction (divide by 100) |

g = 9.80665 m/s² **[Code]**. Air properties are constant everywhere for the whole solve **[Learn: air]**; ρ converts head to pressure and scales duct and tee losses; ν enters only through the Reynolds number.

## 2. Input document (`tools.petrov.re/duct-network/v1`)

Every network case stores the complete document. Fields:

```
{ "schema": "tools.petrov.re/duct-network/v1",      optional; if present it must equal this string
  "air":      { "rho": kg/m3, "nu": m2/s },          ("fluid" accepted as an alias of "air")
  "analysis": { "loadFactor": %, "speedFactor": % },
  "nodes": [ { "id", "name", "x", "y", "z", "demand", "fixed", "p" } ],
  "edges": [ { "id", "name", "type", "a", "b", ...type fields } ] }
```

Node: `z` elevation (m); `demand` (m³/h, positive removes air at the node, negative injects it **[Learn: demand]**); `fixed` (boolean, true = fixed-pressure boundary); `p` gauge total pressure (Pa), used only when `fixed`; `x`, `y` drawing coordinates (no physical meaning, validated only).

Edge (component), drawn from node `a` to node `b`; positive airflow follows a→b **[Learn: palette]**:

| `type` | fields |
|---|---|
| `duct` | `shape` (`rect` or `round`), `W`, `H` (mm, used when rect), `D` (mm, used when round), `L` (m), `eps` (mm), `K` (–) |
| `tee` | `shape`, `W`, `H`, `D` as for a duct, `K` (–). No length, no roughness. |
| `fan` | `P0` shutoff pressure (Pa), `Qrated` (m³/h), `Prated` (Pa), `speed` local speed (%) |
| `damper` | `Qdesign` (m³/h), `dpDesign` (Pa), `opening` (%), `law` (`linear` or `equal`), `target` (m³/h; auto-balance only, no effect on a solve) |
| `grille` | `Qdesign` (m³/h), `dpDesign` (Pa), `n` exponent (–) |

Missing fields take import defaults **[Code]** (all case documents carry every field, so these matter only for reading the format): node `z`, `demand`, `p` = 0, `fixed` = false; duct `shape` rect, `W` 500, `H` 300, `D` 400, `L` 10, `eps` 0.09, `K` 0; tee `K` 1; fan `P0` 650, `Qrated` 5000, `Prated` 430, `speed` 100; damper `Qdesign` 2500, `dpDesign` 55, `opening` 100, `law` linear, `target` 0; grille `Qdesign` 1200, `dpDesign` 35, `n` 2; air ρ 1.204, ν 1.5e-5; `loadFactor` and `speedFactor` 100.

## 3. Network equations

Let λ = loadFactor/100 and σ_g = speedFactor/100. For every component e from a to b with airflow q (m³/s):

**Energy (steady Bernoulli in gauge total pressure plus elevation) [Learn: intro, elevation, boundary; Limitations]:**

  p_a + (ρ − ρ_out) g z_a + Δp_fan,e(q) − Δp_loss,e(q) = p_b + (ρ − ρ_out) g z_b

Every node pressure p (given at fixed nodes, solved at free nodes) is a gauge total pressure relative to the outdoor atmosphere at that node's own elevation z. The conveyed air contributes ρ g z and the outdoor atmosphere −ρ_out g z to the absolute pressure difference, hence (ρ − ρ_out) g z. The page has no separate outdoor-density input, so ρ_out = ρ (the `air.rho` input) and the elevation terms are zero: z does not change any graded value, and two openings at 0 Pa at different heights drive no flow. Buoyancy and stack effect are not modelled.

Δp_fan is zero for every type except `fan`; Δp_loss is zero for `fan`. Δp_loss is odd in q: Δp_loss(q) = sign(q)·|Δp_loss|(|q|), with Δp_loss(0) = 0.

**Continuity at every free node j [Learn: intro, demand, load]:**

  Σ_{e: b=j} q_e − Σ_{e: a=j} q_e − λ·demand_j/3600 = 0

**Fixed node j:** p_j = `p` of the node (given). Its boundary airflow, the net air the boundary supplies into the network, is

  boundary_q_j = λ·demand_j/3600 + Σ_{e: a=j} q_e − Σ_{e: b=j} q_e  **[Code; table heading "Boundary +in"]**

(a demand on a fixed node is allowed and is included).

## 4. Component laws

v = |q|/A. For `shape: round`: A = πD²/4, D_h = D. For `shape: rect`: A = W·H, D_h = 2WH/(W+H) **[Code; ASHRAE Fundamentals, Duct Design]**. Re = v·D_h/ν.

**Duct [Learn: duct]:** |Δp_loss| = (f·L/D_h + K)·ρv²/2, with f = f(Re, ε/D_h) from section 5 and ε = eps/1000 (m).

**Tee / fitting arm [Learn: tee]:** |Δp_loss| = K·ρv²/2, with v from the arm's own section. No friction term. K is an input, not derived from geometry or split ratio.

**Damper [Learn: damper]:** |Δp_loss| = dpDesign·(|q|/Q_d)²/c², Q_d = Qdesign/3600,
o = clamp(opening/100, 0.001, 1) **[Code]**, c = o for `linear`, c = 50^(o−1) for `equal`.
Import refuses openings below 0.1 % (section 8), so the clamp is never active on an accepted document **[Limitations]**. dpDesign is in Pa and is not density-corrected.

**Grille [Learn: grille]:** |Δp_loss| = dpDesign·(|q|/Q_d)^n, Q_d = Qdesign/3600, 1 ≤ n ≤ 3. Not density-corrected.

**Fan [Learn: fan; Limitations; Code for the reverse-flow branch]:** the curve is the fan **total-pressure rise** added to the gauge total pressure of the airflow; P0 and Prated are total pressures (a manufacturer static-pressure curve would need the fan outlet velocity pressure added before entry, which the model does not do). With s = (speed/100)·σ_g, Q_r = Qrated/3600 and a = (P0 − Prated)/Q_r²,

  Δp_fan(q) = P0·s² − a·q·|q|

for every sign of q (for q < 0 the curve continues as P0·s² + a·q²). At s = 1 it passes through (0, P0) and (Q_r, Prated); the speed enters as s² on the shutoff term only, which is the affinity law dp ∝ n² for this curve shape. Zero-pressure runout: q_ro = sqrt(P0·s²/a).

## 5. Friction factor [Learn: duct; Limitations; Code for the blend]

With R = ε/D_h:

- Re ≤ 0: f = 0 (zero airflow, zero loss).
- 0 < Re ≤ 2000: f = 64/Re (Hagen–Poiseuille).
- Re ≥ 4000: f = f_SJ(Re, R) = 0.25 / [log10( R/3.7 + 5.74/Re^0.9 )]²  (Swamee & Jain 1976).
- 2000 < Re < 4000: t = (Re − 2000)/2000, s = t²(3 − 2t), f = (64/Re)·(1 − s) + f_SJ(Re, R)·s. This smoothstep is a numerical bridge, not a published transition model **[Limitations]**.

Swamee–Jain is published for 1e-6 ≤ R ≤ 1e-2 and 5e3 ≤ Re ≤ 1e8; the formula is applied unchanged outside that box (the page warns, section 9). log10 is the decimal logarithm.

The `swamee_jain_grid` case evaluates this f(Re, R) directly at the stored (Re, rel) points, with rel = R; no network is involved.

## 6. Solution and scaling (how precise the page's numbers are)

The page solves the system of section 3 by damped Newton with a central-difference Jacobian **[Learn: solver]** and stops when the infinity norm of the **scaled** residual is ≤ 2e-9 **[Learn: solver]**, the rows being scaled as follows **[Code]**:

- continuity rows divided by q_s (m³/s): q_s = max(1e-5, D) where D = max over nodes of |λ·demand/3600| and over fans of |s·Q_r|, when D > 1e-9; otherwise (no demand, no fan) q_s is the largest single-component airflow that the span of fixed-node heads would drive through that component alone, floored at 1e-5;
- energy rows written in metres of air head (Pa divided by ρg) and divided by h_s = max(5, max over fixed nodes |p/(ρg)|, max over nodes |(ρ − ρ_out)·z/ρ| (zero, since ρ_out = ρ), max over fans |P0·s²/(ρg)|).

So each page energy equation holds to about 2e-9·h_s·ρg Pa and each continuity equation to about 2e-9·q_s m³/s. A reference converged far below that will differ from the page by the page's own residual, not by a model difference; set tolerances from these figures. If 60 iterations pass with the residual still above 2e-9 but at or below 2e-6, the page reports the result as unconverged (status `unconverged`); above 2e-6 it refuses (`no_convergence`).

The networks here are monotone (every loss law is increasing and odd in q; every fan curve is decreasing in q), so each accepted, referenced case has one steady solution.

## 7. Analysis factors

- λ (loadFactor) multiplies every nodal demand, fixed nodes included. It does not touch fans, dampers or grilles **[Learn: load]**. Valid 0–150 %.
- σ_g (speedFactor) multiplies the local speed of every fan **[Learn: speed]**. Valid 40–120 %.

## 8. Refusals and their kinds

A refusal produces no solution. The graded output is `status` (`refused_import` or `refused_solve`) and `refusal_kind`. Every refusal document in `cases.json` has exactly one defect.

**On import** (opening the file) the page refuses, in this order **[Code; messages quoted]**:

| check | kind |
|---|---|
| file text is not valid JSON (message "The file is not valid JSON: " followed by the browser's parser text) | `invalid_json` |
| not an object, or `nodes`/`edges` not arrays — "Invalid network file" | `invalid_file` |
| `schema` present and not `tools.petrov.re/duct-network/v1` | `schema` |
| a numeric field present but not a finite number, or `fixed` present but not boolean — "<field> must be finite/boolean" | `field_type` |
| more than 1000 nodes or 3000 components | `file_too_large` |
| ρ outside 0.2–2 kg/m³ | `air_density` |
| ν ≤ 0 | `viscosity` |
| loadFactor outside 0–150 % | `load_factor` |
| speedFactor outside 40–120 % | `speed_factor` |
| node id not matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,63}$` | `invalid_node_id` |
| duplicate node id | `duplicate_node_id` |
| node `x` outside 0–1000 or `y` outside 0–620 | `outside_canvas` |
| component id not matching the same pattern | `invalid_component_id` |
| duplicate component id | `duplicate_component_id` |
| endpoint `a` or `b` not a node id, or `a` = `b` | `endpoints` |
| `type` not one of duct, fan, damper, grille, tee | `unsupported_type` |
| duct/tee `shape` not rect/round | `shape` |
| round D ≤ 0, or rect W ≤ 0 or H ≤ 0 | `dimension` |
| duct L ≤ 0, eps < 0 or K < 0 | `duct_params` |
| tee K < 0 | `tee_params` |
| fan: not (P0 > Prated ≥ 0 and Qrated > 0) | `fan_rating` |
| fan local speed outside 1–150 % | `fan_speed` |
| damper Qdesign ≤ 0 or dpDesign ≤ 0 | `damper_params` |
| damper opening outside 0.1–100 % | `damper_opening` |
| damper target < 0 | `damper_params` |
| damper law not linear/equal | `damper_law` |
| grille Qdesign ≤ 0, dpDesign ≤ 0, or n outside 1–3 | `grille_params` |

**On solve** (the document imported, the solve is pressed), additionally and in this order:

| check | kind |
|---|---|
| fewer than 2 nodes | `too_few_nodes` |
| no component | `no_components` |
| a node with no component attached — "Node X is isolated." | `isolated_node` |
| components + free nodes > 600 — "…nonlinear unknowns; the browser dense solver is limited to 600." | `unknown_limit` |
| a connected part of the network containing no fixed node — "…has no fixed-pressure reference." | `no_reference` |
| solver: singular Jacobian, failed line search, non-finite initial residual | `solver_failed` |
| scaled residual > 2e-6 after 60 iterations | `no_convergence` |

Isolation, the unknown count and the pressure reference are not checked on import: such a file imports and is refused at the solve. 600 unknowns exactly is accepted **[Learn: solver; Limitations]**. `imported_counts` (graded in `unknown_count_limit`) is the number of nodes and components the page holds after import; nothing may be dropped.

## 9. Warnings (solved cases)

After a successful solve the page lists warnings **[Message; Learn: duct, fan]**. Graded as a set of `{kind, components}` with component ids sorted; one entry per kind; the empty set when none.

For each component of type **duct** with Re > 2000 (tees are never checked):
- 2000 < Re < 4000 → `transition_blend` ("Transition region (2000<Re<4000), interpolated not resolved: …");
- otherwise, if Re < 5000 or Re > 1e8 or ε/D_h < 1e-6 or ε/D_h > 1e-2 → `sj_range` ("Outside the published Swamee–Jain range (5e3≤Re≤1e8, 1e-6≤ε/Dh≤1e-2): …"). ε = 0 gives ε/D_h = 0 and is warned. ε/D_h is formed as (eps/1000)/D_h in double precision; ε/D_h exactly 1e-6 or exactly 1e-2 is inside the range.

For each **fan**: q < 0 → `fan_reverse`; q > 1.001·q_ro → `fan_runout`.


## 10. Graded output keys

| key | unit | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | enum | `solved`, `unconverged`, `refused_import`, `refused_solve`; `evaluated` for the friction grid and the documentation case |
| `refusal_kind` | enum | section 8 |
| `warnings` | set | section 9 |
| `edge.<id>.q` | m³/s | airflow, positive a→b |
| `edge.<id>.dp_loss` | Pa | signed Δp_loss(q) (non-fan components) |
| `edge.<id>.fan_dp` | Pa | Δp_fan(q) at the solved q |
| `edge.<id>.v` | m/s | |q|/A (ducts, tees) |
| `edge.<id>.Re` | – | v·D_h/ν (ducts) |
| `edge.<id>.f` | – | Darcy friction factor at that Re and ε/D_h (ducts) |
| `node.<id>.p` | Pa | gauge total pressure (given for fixed nodes, solved for free ones) |
| `node.<id>.boundary_q` | m³/s | section 3 (fixed nodes) |
| `imported_counts` | {nodes, edges} | section 8 |
| `f.<i>` | – | f(Re_i, rel_i) at grid point i (`swamee_jain_grid`) |
| `doc.<lang>.label.<P0\|Prated>.basis` | enum | pressure basis the rendered inspector label of that fan field names at `?lang=<lang>`: `total`, `static`, `mixed` (both named) or `unstated` |
| `doc.<lang>.limitations.fan_basis` | enum | the same, for the first clause (up to the first ";") of the sentence in manifest `limitations[<lang>]` that describes the fan curve |

The documentation case (`input_kind: "page-text"`) grades what the page says about the fan basis in each of en, uk, de, nl, fr, es, pl; per §4 the stated basis is the total-pressure rise.

A case of `input_kind: "document-sequence"` is a list of independent documents; each step is solved cold on its own and its keys are prefixed with `<step>/`. `example_damper_throttling` grades the per-step flows; the monotonicity of the E4 branch, fan and parallel-branch flows over the openings is a property to check on the reference values as well as on the page values.

## 11. Literature

- P.K. Swamee & A.K. Jain, "Explicit equations for pipe-flow problems", ASCE J. Hydraulics Div. 102(HY5) (1976) 657–664 — the turbulent friction factor and its stated range.
- C.F. Colebrook, J. Inst. Civ. Eng. 11 (1939) 133–156 — the implicit law Swamee–Jain approximates; for quantifying the approximation only, never as the graded law.
- Hagen–Poiseuille laminar friction, f = 64/Re.
- ASHRAE Handbook — Fundamentals, Duct Design chapter: hydraulic diameter of a rectangular duct 2WH/(W+H); local loss Δp = K·ρv²/2.
- H. Cross, "Analysis of Flow in Networks of Conduits or Conductors", Univ. of Illinois Eng. Exp. Station Bulletin 286 (1936) — loop-correction method, suitable as a second, structurally different solver.
- Fan affinity law, pressure ∝ (speed)², applied to the two-point quadratic curve of section 4.

## 12. Ambiguities and points where the documents disagree

- **A1 — ε/D_h bounds of the warning.** Learn, limitations, the warning sentence and §9 agree on 1e-6 ≤ ε/D_h ≤ 1e-2. The comparison is on the double-precision value of (eps/1000)/D_h; `sj_eps_bounds` uses D = 1000 mm so that 0.001 mm and 10 mm give exactly 1e-6 and 1e-2.
- **A2 — 4000 ≤ Re < 5000.** The friction law switches to Swamee–Jain at 4000 while the published range starts at 5000; such a duct uses f_SJ and is warned `sj_range` (R3).
- **A3 — inclusive bounds.** Re = 2000 is laminar; Re = 4000 is pure Swamee–Jain; `transition_blend` is the open interval (2000, 4000); `sj_range` uses strict Re < 5000, Re > 1e8, ε/D_h < 1e-6 and ε/D_h > 1e-2. No case sits exactly on a Re bound; `sj_eps_bounds` sits exactly on both ε/D_h bounds.
- **A4 — outdoor density.** The documents state no outdoor-air density input, and the page has none; ρ_out = ρ follows. A future separate outdoor density would make (ρ − ρ_out) g z non-zero; no case depends on that.
- **A5 — fan pressure basis.** Learn, labels, limitations and report state the curve as the fan total-pressure rise. The `doc.*.basis` classification uses per-language keyword sets (total: total/повн/total|gesamt/totale|totaal/totale/total/całkow; static: static/статич/statisch/statisch/statique/estátic/statyczn); a text naming both is `mixed`.
- **A6 — fan curve for reverse flow.** The documents say only that reverse flow is an extrapolation; the code continues the curve as P0·s² − a·q·|q|, i.e. rising for q < 0 (section 4).
- **A7 — damper and grille losses are density-independent;** duct and tee losses scale with ρ. Relevant to `single_round_duct` (non-default ρ) only where dampers or grilles would appear; none do there.
- **A8 — the damper opening clamp** (0.001 floor) is unreachable on an accepted document; it is stated for completeness.
- **A9 — unused geometry fields.** A rect duct carries `D` and a round one `W`, `H`; the unused ones have no effect.
- **A10 — `invalid_json` text** is the browser's parser message and varies by engine; only the kind is graded.
- **A11 — check order.** Sections 8's tables give the order the page applies; with one defect per document the order does not decide any graded kind.
- **A12 — page precision.** Section 6 gives the page's own convergence criterion; a tolerance tighter than the page's stopping rule tests the stopping rule, not the model.

concerns.concern: The curve is now stated everywhere as the fan total-pressure rise, which is consistent with its use in a total-pressure energy balance. Remaining note: a user entering a manufacturer static-pressure curve must add the fan outlet velocity pressure first; the model has no outlet area, so it cannot do or check that.

tolerance.rule: pass if |page - ref| <= max(rel * |ref|, abs) where abs is the per-key value in each case's abs_tolerance_from_page_stopping_rule (when present) or the default abs below

q.why: page continuity rows hold to 2e-9*q_s and energy rows to 2e-9*h_s*rho*g; the per-key abs value is 10x the first-order bound |J_s^-1|*2e-9 of the page's scaled system at the solution, so it covers near-zero-flow branches.

dp_loss.why: energy rows hold to 2e-9*h_s*rho*g (>= 1.2e-7 Pa at h_s 5 m); per-key abs propagates the q bound through d(loss)/dq.

v.why: v = |q|/A: same relative accuracy as q.

Re.why: Re = v Dh/nu: same relative accuracy as q.

f.why: |dlnf/dlnRe| <= 1 on every branch, so f carries at most the relative error of q.

node.p.why: free-node pressures inherit the energy-row residual 2e-9*h_s*rho*g accumulated along a path; fixed nodes are inputs (exact).

boundary_q.why: sum of incident flows: abs = sum of their q bounds.

f.<i> (friction grid).why: closed-form evaluation in double precision; only round-off differs (log10 and pow).
